summary: Serratiopeptidase (serrapeptase) is a proteolytic enzyme derived from Serratia bacteria, used as an adjunct anti-inflammatory and anti-edema agent for swelling, pain and secretion clearance after surgery, trauma, and in ENT/dental and respiratory conditions. It is formulated as enteric-coated tablets to survive gastric acid. Evidence of clinical benefit is limited and it is not FDA-approved.
indications: Adjunctive reduction of inflammation, swelling and pain after surgery or trauma
ENT inflammatory conditions (sinusitis, otitis, pharyngitis) as an adjunct
Reduction of viscosity of respiratory and other secretions as an adjunct

moa: Serratiopeptidase is a proteolytic (peptidase) enzyme that hydrolyzes proteins in inflammatory exudates, thinning viscous secretions and breaking down bradykinin and other inflammatory mediators. This is proposed to reduce tissue edema, facilitate drainage and lessen pain, accounting for its use as an anti-inflammatory and anti-edema adjunct. The precise clinical mechanism in humans is not fully characterized.

missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule; do not double the dose.
overdose: There is no specific antidote and human overdose data are limited. Manage supportively and symptomatically, with attention to gastrointestinal symptoms, possible hypersensitivity and bleeding. Discontinue the drug.
